newsitem.title: DENMARK: FLS says U.K. aerospace unit recovering.
newsitem.headline: FLS says U.K. aerospace unit recovering.

text.p: Danish engineering group FLS Industries said on Tuesday that its loss-making British-based FLS Aerospace unit cut losses significantly in 1996 and was expected to show further improvement in 1997.
In its group annual accounts for 1996 the company said that FLS Aerospace made a pre-tax loss of 86 million crowns, compared to a loss of 146 million the year before.
"Even though FLS Aerospace Holdings made a loss -- of the amount expected -- in 1996, the year was satisfactory in many ways," the report said.

"The client base was broadened and during the year several long-term contracts were signed, meaning that at the start of 1997 the firm has its strongest order book ever. In 1997 the progress of recent years is expected to continue," it added.

The unit, which provides aircraft maintenance and engineering services, last month signed a three-year, stg 25 million contract with British Airways to service aircraft at Gatwick, Manchester and Stansted airports.
FLS said at the time that the order allowed it to reopen its Gatwick hangar, closed for the past four years due to lack of business.
